subject: general
question: A merchant gains 20% after allowing a discount of 10% on the marked price. Find his profit percentage if no discount were allowed.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let CP = 100

Gain 20% ⇒ SP = 120

This SP is after 10% discount ⇒ MP × 0.9 = 120

⇒ MP = 120 ÷ 0.9 = 133.33

Profit without discount = (133.33 − 100)% = 33.33%

**∴ Answer = 33.33%**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Discount = 10%

Gain after discount = 20%

**Formula:**

SP = CP × (1 + gain%)

SP = MP × (1 − discount%)

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let CP = 100

⇒ Gain 20% ⇒ SP = 100 + 20 = 120

⇒ SP = MP × 0.9

⇒ 120 = MP × 0.9

⇒ MP = 120 ÷ 0.9 = 133.33

⇒ Profit without discount = (MP − CP) ÷ CP × 100

⇒ = (133.33 − 100) = 33.33%

**∴ Final Answer: 33.33%**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

**Profit Formula:** Profit% = (SP − CP) ÷ CP × 100

**Discount Formula:** SP = MP × (1 − discount)

**Shortcut Base:** Assume CP = 100 for faster solving
